sentence: This project studies how alcohol and a calorie-dense diet disrupt the processes of liver mitochondria and the handling of lipids.
This project uses genomic data from leukemia patients who had a stem cell transplant to find neoantigens that could be treatment targets.
This project studies how primate lentiviruses adapted to humans and how human cells resist infection by these viruses.
This project studies why cancers such as pancreatic cancer and glioma resist radiation therapy, looking at DNA repair, immunogenicity and tumor metabolism.
This project builds machine learning tools to design vaccines against influenza viruses and tests the designed immunogens in vitro and in vivo.
This project builds an imaging informatics platform that lets cancer researchers capture, analyze and share imaging data.
This project tests how medulloblastoma, a brain tumor in children, resists treatment, using in vivo perturb-seq and preclinical therapeutics.
This project studies how transcription factors and somatic mutations reinforce each other to shape the genome during aging and clonal hematopoiesis.
This project studies how cancer-associated fibroblasts change the response of bladder cancer to treatment and builds a gene signature to sort patients.
This project provides bioinformatic analyses of single cell, spatial transcriptomics and RNA-seq data to help researchers understand digestive diseases.
This project builds a platform that combines biophysical measurements and computational modelling to decode and design the free energy landscapes of proteins.
This project studies how chronic inflammation affects hematopoietic stem cells and the bone marrow niche cells that support them during aging.
This project studies changes in sphingolipid metabolism in acute myelogenous leukemia cells, using mass spectrometry and drug delivery strategies.
This project studies whether changes in gene activity in parvalbumin interneurons match their physiological and morphological properties in the prefrontal and visual cortices.
This project studies how cytoskeletal motor proteins move specific RNAs to their destinations inside cells, using a tool for spatial transcriptomics.
This project develops inhibitors that block essential viral enzymes made by flaviviruses.
This project tests whether a nanofibrillar aligned collagen scaffold placed at the time of lymph resection can prevent secondary lymphedema.
This project coordinates studies of the epigenetic programs, signaling pathways and metabolic adaptations that make pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma resist therapy.
This project studies ways to prevent cancer, control symptoms and support people living after treatment, using trials and artificial intelligence.
